This is a really deep topic for me. My family has been deeply affected by guns in both positive and negative ways, (Hunting, suicides, etc.) and I spent most of my school life being terrified of shootings, being bullied and beaten, and so many other instances of physical violence. 

    As a kid, I was VERY violent due to mostly social factors. Meaning, it wasn't the fiction I got, but the bullying and violence I got from other people my age that caused me to act violently. 
    My siblings and I fought sometimes, of course, but overall we solved our issues and desire for fighting WITH games. If we wanted to brawl it out, we played smash bros to decide who was the winner or did obstacle courses in our backyard. 
     I mostly played exploratory, story-based, games such as Zelda, and I watched shows such as Avatar the Last Airbender, both of which contain fantasy violence. But, I also got my fair share of brawling games, Mortal combat, and "normal" violence in Media, alongside learning about 9/11 and other terror attacks or wars non-stop.
     Personally, those media influences of shows and games actually helped me because I learned how to dodge and evade attacks when I got bullied. I actively hid and tried to avoid physical conflict and contact at that younger age. While some of my violent streaks and worries did spill over as I got older and as I went into middle school, i.e. came out more as violent acts rather than hiding, and I was always on high alert and ready for a fight, I was able to overcome it because of social obstacles. I went from defensive, to violent, to non-violent. 
     My close friend, now best friend, told me back then that if I didn't stop acting out that way, that she wouldn't be friends with me anymore. That social factor helped me. I was able to step away, take a look at myself, and stop hurting people around me physically. I was able to stop acting like a wild dog that had been abused, and more like a rescue puppy.
     Do I still play games to this day? YES! Absolutely! My best friend, the peace lover, also plays games. She grew up on Horror and shooter games to be exact. I have never seen her hurt ANYONE, not even a punch. So...those games didn't change her either. She just found them fun and interesting, without having a desire to hurt anyone, despite the hard times and situations that made her life far more adverse than mine. 

    So, with the utmost certainty, I can say that in my experience, video games did not cause me to act out violently, nor did they totally cure my violence. They were simply a tool I used as escapism, a completely separate part of my life from my social influences, which changed and turned me from a violent and hurt individual to someone who healed and wears the scars of that time proudly. To someone who now follows non-violent communication vows as a part of my lifestyle. Video games were in a completely different ballpark physiologically when it came to how I acted and if I used violence. What caused all of it for me was social surroundings and attitudes. It was the atmosphere I was in that changed me over and over again. 

    I was a fighter when I had to be, when I needed to not get bloodied and bruised too often. Then, when that changed and went away, and I was no longer tormented in a violent environment, I was able to change and become a better person and communicator. So...whenever someone blames games, I have to just look them in the eye and disagree. Firmly. Social surroundings are what shape a person FAR more than the media they ingest, especially when the two conflicts with one another, and especially if that individual is able to distinguish fiction from reality.

Thank you, Theorist Team. I enjoyed doing this so much, especially this final challenge. Everything was so cleverly made, and as you said in your videos on this, it's extremely evident how much time and effort you all have put into this experience. I really enjoyed all the references, all the humor, and the gratitude sprinkled into this last gate especially. So thank you for this incredible experience.
To break down Gate 7's keys, I want to talk about what really stood out to me. Designing the whole thing like a text based adventure game, using the URLs as player moves, was simply genius. I never would have thought of doing that, and yet you made it work really well. The Drama Llama mazes were fun. I wasn't too challenging, but it did have cute and witty dialogue, and impressive designs. It was a really good warm up for the difficulty to come. I also really enjoyed the nonographs and got extremely excited when I realized what they were. I had been playing a lot of Pokemon Pixel, so I felt like I had been training for that very moment. Plus, I found it really endearing that person messages to Kynk were put into the game. I've got to say though, it took me SO long to figure out what to do with the dead end. It was really tricky to figure it out especially when I was trying every possible way it could have been interpreted. But when I did find out what I had to do, I thought it was extremely clever; instructions hidden in plain sight. I'm not entirely sure what triggered the fourth key's appearing, but I was extremely relieved when it did. The mini games took a bit of trial and error, thought, and a lot of loading, but it was still fun. I'm really bad with interpreting visual Morse code (having an extremely hard time differentiating a dash from a dot) but I got through it. The narrowing down of video-games was a long and grueling process, but felt oddly satisfying in the end. And the last challenge was so incredibly genius. Though it took me a very long time to complete (mainly because I didn't realize there were final clues at the end of every gate), I had a blast solving it. The final video at the end was bittersweet. I enjoyed the ARG so much, but now it's over. So just, thank you so so much Team Theorists for making this incredible journey.

The below comment is from the channel Sumwan who did an incredible job critiquing this episode. ***Original Text from Sumwan***
I've seen this claim many times and it really does not make any sense. Not only does it contradict evidence in the game but it is very misleading. I'll go through the points one by one and explain why:

6:35 “We too might be in the ranks of a higher being” 

The Knight is the child of the Pale King and the White Lady, who are both higher beings. It makes sense that the Knight is able to read these higher being tablets. This doesn't mean that the Pale King IS the Knight.

7:20 “Does it really sound like we're just some failed experiment cast into the depths of this world?”

No, it doesn't sound like that. The Vessels are the children of the Pale King and the White Lady who are born from eggs in the Abyss, which gave them a Shade. The Vessels are not just “failed experiments”. 

8:12 “This poem is addressed to the Pale King”

It literally says “elegy for HALLOWNEST”. This poem is about Hallownest. “Under palest watch” refers to the Pale King, but the “you”, is most definitely Hallownest. 

8:30 “In the beginning of the game's lore, all bugs were basically a hive mind controlled by the moth god Radiance”

This information is not supported by anything. Only the Radiance's descendants, the moth tribe, worshipped her. Nowhere is it stated that the Radiance controlled everything else. The Mantis Tribe, the Mosskin, Deepnest, and the Hive were all separate tribes and already had minds before the Pale King. 

8:51 “This isn't just a poem about the Pale King, it is directed TO the Pale King”

It is about Hallownest and it is direct to Hallownest (elegy for Hallownest).

8:55 “What do we see appear on screen just moments later? Our Knight”

After the poem we see THE HOLLOW KNIGHT, not the Knight. The Knight scene appears after we see the Radiance break out of the Hollow Knight. Team Cherry is NOT drawing a parallel between the Knight and the Pale King. The poem is about Hallownest. It is FOR Hallownest. And the scene with the Knight does not appear right after the poem.

10:27 “Elderbug says we are seeking our dreams in perhaps a very literal sense.”

The context of this sentence matters. Elderbug is talking about how all the previous travellers went down into Hallownest to follow their dreams. He does not actually know if the Knight has any “dreams” themselves.

11:00 “Elderbug wondering if he's seen a ghost is another potentially clever play on words” 

No it's not. Elderbug is just referring to how he thought maybe he didn't see anyone pass him because the Knight left so quickly. This dialogue has no other meaning besides that. 

11:36 “White Lady: Is it more than simply a Vessel? I almost feel like I'm once again in the presence of my beloved Wyrm”

The White Lady only says this because the Knight is wearing the Kingsoul. The Kingsoul reminds her of the Pale King, not the Knight themselves. Also, the White Lady literally calls the Knight her spawn when they visit her with Grimmchild equipped: “Success then for the scarlet heart, and irony, to use my spawn to grow its own.” Are you saying that the White Lady gave birth to her own husband? 

11:46 “Your noble bearing reminds me of our dear King” 

No surprise there since the Knight is the child of the Pale King.

12:05 “The bugs in White Palace bowing as you approach them is just screaming that you're the king”

White Palace is a whole other issue, but this is really not concrete evidence. Also their dream nail dialogue makes no sense if it refers to the Knight.

12:19 “10/10 Royal Retainers can't be wrong. You are royalty” 

You're actually right there. The Knight IS royalty, since they're the child of the King. Not because they ARE the King.

13:28 “This line of “more transformation” seems to imply that the Pale King's death would only lead to yet another form”

Not really. Bardoon says that the Pale King's death in Kingdom's Edge was not an actual death, but that it was more like a transformation. This does not mean that the Pale King can transform again after he became his bug shape. A caterpillar transforming into a butterfly also cannot transform into another being again. 

13:49 “It's an ancient force that opposes the blinding light of [the Radiance]” 

Not just the Radiance's light, but the Pale King's too. He is referred to as a light in multiple places:

The Seer:
“But another light appeared in our world... A wyrm that took the form of a king.”

The Pale King calls himself a light in the throne room lore tablet:
“No blazing kin. Only one light shall shine against the dark.”

As does the Teacher’s Archives lore tablet:
“-KINGLIGHT-EM-GROWTH-INKIND-FLOW-ALLTHINK-ENFIELD”

Other bugs talk about the Pale King emanating light:
“Though even its pure aura is no match for the light of our dear King.” (Eternal Emilitia)
“I've heard he was a glorious bug to behold, bright and radiant in visage, so much so it hurt to look at him.” (Last/Old Stag)
“That lingering power alone was beacon enough to draw Us to Hallownest. How bright it must have been to mortal bug stood before it.” (Godseeker)

14:45 “The Pale King used Void to fight time itself. He wants to use the Void to attain eternal life. He births himself as a Void-based creature”

Not literally time. Time here is capitalized, and it is more likely to just refer to the Radiance. Locking up the Radiance is generally seen as being what has caused the Kingdom to remain in a stasis: 
“Bear witness to the last and only civilisation, the eternal Kingdom. Hallownest”” 
“Eternity in promise and charge in progeny cursed.” 
“Now this Kingdom's stasis becomes the Wyrm's legacy.” 
“Though this hive exists within Hallownest, we play no part in its attempt at perpetuation.” 

It is not literally time. He is a higher being, he does not need to use the Void to “achieve eternal life”. Not to mention that the Void opposes his own powers too (see previous point).

15:25 “It seems to suggest that this egg [in White Palace] is where version 1.0 of the Pale King hatched  into its upgraded form” 

It does not. The Pale King became his current bug form in the Cast-Off shell. The Wanderer's Journal even mentions that too on page 111: “Deep within the maw of the [Cast-Off Shell], a pale, broken egg of some sort hints at such a rebirth.” Not only that, but the egg of the Knight in the Abyss would be DEADLY for the Pale King. Void opposes his power, it would simply kill him if he were to become corrupted by the Void like the eggs of the Vessels were. 

15:40 “Elsewhere in White Palace there is a nursery playing this song on the music box (shade theme). The sound that accompanies our Knight's past life coincides with the same sound from a nursery housed in the Pale King's palace.” 

Yes, this is true, but not because of the reason you're describing. It's because the Hollow Knight grew up in White Palace (see Path of Pain scene). This nursery was probably for them. And since the Hollow Knight is a Vessel too, it makes sense that the Shade theme place for that area.

16:21 “The existence of a connection between our Knight and the Pale King seems undeniable” 

Yes, it is undeniable. The Knight is the child of the Pale King.

18:13 “In cut dialogue that was datamined from the game, it shows that the Hollow Knight says “father”. 

Cut dialogue is not evidence. The "Father?" is cut dream nail dialogue. It was cut for a reason. We don't know when this line was written, in which context it would be used exactly, maybe the Hollow Knight's fight was different at the time, etc. 

19:20 “Losing his memory helps make him purely hollow”

It does not. Quirrel lost his memory and this does not happen to him. Not to mention that the Knight is not hollow. There are multiple places where the Knight is said to have a will: 

Steel Soul Jinn: "...It refuses to trade...? It has a will... all Its own." 
Void Heart description: "Unifies the void under the bearer's will." 
Description of a pure Vessel: "No will to break."

Lastly I'm going to address some fundamental problems with this entire theory that you did not address or seem to have forgotten about. 

The most obvious evidence that contradicts that the Pale King is the Knight is that the Knight and the Pale King are both seen at the same time. This is during the Birthplace memory cutscene where the Hollow Knight is led out of the Abyss by the Pale King. This is a memory of the Knight themselves since the Knight dreamnails their own reflection to access this memory. Furthermore, the achievement for acquiring Void Heart also says: 

"Remember the past and unite the Abyss"

This supports the fact that it is the Knight’s memory. Therefore, the Pale King cannot be the Knight, since they were alive at the same time.

Secondly, the Knight is the child of the Pale King, not a transformation. The lore tablet to the right of the throne in White Palace says that the Vessels are the progeny of the Pale King, and the Pale King also says that the Vessels are "born of God and Void", the God obviously referring to him and the White Lady who are both higher beings. Since the Knight is the child of the Pale King (and the White Lady), the Pale King cannot BE the Knight. 

None of the points that were brought up align with the evidence that is in the game, and it even contradicts it in various places. To put it quite simply, the Knight is NOT the Pale King.

To my understanding, it isn't so much that Darkrai actively uses its nightmare powers as a means of self-defense, although they do certainly end up working in that manner in a roundabout way, but rather that it is a _constant_ force that emits from it, affecting everything in the area around it with the horrible, inescapable nightmares it is unfortunately so well known for. (as potentially indicated by its permanently active Ability Bad Dreams, which always takes effect as soon as a Pokémon falls asleep near it, and begins doing damage to them every turn) 

Darkrai, fully aware of how its presence harms others, actively tries to prevent scenarios like this from happening by staying as far away from other living beings as it can, and as an added countermeasure, it seems that they also try to keep their territory near an area where a Crescelia can be found, since their feathers are the only thing that can save someone once they've succumb to Darkrai's involuntarily active nightmare field. This is potentially alluded to by the only location you can legitimately find Darkrai in the main series games, Newmoon Island, being set up incredibly far from any of the Sinnoh mainland's most populated areas, yet still suspiciously within close proximity to its counterpart, Fullmoon Island, which is both noticeably less barren than its mirrored counterpart that is home to Darkrai, but is where you also just so happen find the Crescelia who gives you the feather needed to save Eldritch's son)

So if I were to hazard a guess, I would say that Unova's Ghost Girl wasn't trapped in her nightmare with malicious intent, but rather she happened to come within the range of the nightmare field that was being emitted by a Darkrai who happened to find its way to a then-secluded portion of the Unova region, leaving her as yet another unintentional victim to Darkrai's unfortunate circumstances, much like Eldritch's son (who perhaps was simply sailing with his father before succumbing to the nightmare, and happened to fall asleep when they were in too close of a proximity to Newmoon Island during the trip), but this time without the help of a Player Character to venture out and save them like the case of Eldritch and his son…

8:08 Okay, when I first saw these different things here, this was one of my first thoughts. You see, I'm very interested in the idea of genetic algorithms, and how virtually anything with modifiable data and a cost function can be optimized using genetic algorithms. Anyways, when I saw this, the general balance of "good runs" and "bad runs" , coupled with there being many of them, made me immediately recognize this as a genetic algorithm in play here. Also note that the same exact thing happened with the recordings, and how they were seperated into generations.
   However, given that genetic algorithms are so far removed from things like child abuse and spiritual imprisonment in the game, I found it unlikely that it was true. So, I started thinking about whether it may actually be many people being trapped in the game, and that in this menu you're capable of seeing what everyone is doing. But that theory was destroyed when Paul took the body of one of the players, leaving me utterly confused at what was going on here. As for the recordings? Well, I thought that they were real people's souls trapped within the game. Instead of having generations of AI, there would be generations of people, with the best person of each generation moving onto the next.
Where am I going with this? Well, once you started leading up to saying that these things are genetic algorithms at play here, I started feeling an overwhelming sense of "I knew it!". So, it's nice to know that I really was right the first time.

Just because I say he's a villain doesn't mean that he's evil or has bad intentions. I mean it as he's a THREAT. That said, I've changed the title to avoid confusion.

Regarding Dyna Blade: Him helping the children after the scene I showed doesn't change the point -- he beat up someone BEFORE learning the whole story, like I tried to make clear in the script. Seeing that scene, he beats up the mom, THEN sees the kids, gives the screen a "cha-ching" gesture and steals them away, feeds them and teaches them to fly...stuff the MOTHER should be doing but can't because she was injured. I get it: Dyna "forgives" him in Revenge of Meta Knight...the same way Landia does in Return to Dream Land, but I see that more as plot convenience because Kirby is the "good guy," or them realizing they have to fight the "true" evil. But think about Kirby;s ACTIONS...if someone just came up to you and started beating you up for no apparent cause, would YOU forgive the person? See them as a hero? Probably not. And don't forget that EVERYONE he fights along the way is in NO WAY connected to the battle between him and Dyna...they're innocents caught in the middle.

Kirby's Avalanche: In both Epic Yarn and the original Kirby's Dream Land manual (those are the ones I can think of offhand, but there might be more), Kirby actually speaks English...or something that translates to English, so I think comments throwing these lines out as invalid might be premature. Yes, the game is non-canon, which I acknowledge, but the idea that Kirby ONLY speaks "poyo" isn't necessarily true...or it can be assumed that ALL of Avalanche's lines are translated poyo.

And yes, I know Avalanche is a version of puyo puyo...it was a joke. Obviously it's not a Candy Crush mod since, if nothing else, Candy Crush came DECADES later.

Absolutely. But he's still a threat.

In Canada, the dispersement of assets is typically done by an officer of the court called a Bankruptcy trustee (who is obligated to act in the best interest of the creditors). In the event of bankruptcy priority works as follows 

1) Unpaid suppliers (irrelevant in this case) 
2) SECURED Creditors -> Creditors who loaned using a specific asset for collateral (for example, the collateral was the building). These creditors have first access to that building.
3) Preferred Creditors -> the most relevant point for preferred creditors is:  "Includes up to 6 months unpaid employee wages"
4) Unsecured General Creditors -> These people have last dibs on the assets.

As a finance and accounting university student, I literally mumbled to myself: did Ally literally just forget what Bad Debt Expense is?

They aren't losing anything. Banks and other businesses that have Receivables on their books have something called Allowance For Doubtful Accounts (ADA). At the beginning of their financial period, they estimate how much of the money owed to them won't end up being paid. Then they change the ADA accordingly, balancing it with Bad Debt Expense. When it is determined that a debt will not be repaid, it is written off. To the bank, this is an expense, not a loss.

Allow me to explain the fundamental difference between an expense and a loss. An expense is an everyday cost of doing business, it's something you pay on a regular basis. For example, a coffee shop would have to pay salaries to their employees. Since their employees are directly related to making them money and salaries are something paid on a regular basis, this is an expense. A loss is not a normal cost of doing business. It's a loss of money that isn't related to the process of making revenue. For example, if a coffee shop buys a coffee maker for $100 and then sells it for $80, that's a loss of $20.

The difference between this money for the bank and the YouTubers is that this is a typical expense for the bank, Bad Debt Expense, but it is a loss for the YouTubers. Those are NOT equivalent. Smh

MatPat, first YouTube comment here! As a researcher in molecular biology, just a quick note in case future videos contain CRISPR related concepts. The mechanism you described is exactly right, but only as bacterial defense against viruses. Eukaryotes (plants, animals, etc.) don't use this form of viral protection, we have much more complex mechanisms. The CRISPR system used in research is the bacterial response to viruses that can be injected into eukaryotes. All the enzymes still function the same way, but we don't actually possess them ourselves. When using CRISPR on animals, it is necessary to inject the CAS-9 enzyme as well, so far that's the only one that's had great success, though there are a dozen or so others. This doesn't at all discount your content, just a forwarding of information for future use in your videos. Thanks for all the great content here and on Film Theory!

The issue with using rabies virus as a way to create a zombie virus is that rabies victims can't drink or eat properly, you essentially end up with a "zombie" that will die out in a matter of days if not hours due to dehydration and starvation! 28 Days Later was pretty darn accurate to show how unsuccessful a realistic zombie outbreak would be. Also infected type zombies are easy to deal with and contain, they don't require 5+ headshots to bring down like in RE2, in fact they'll be easier to kill than regular humans due to being weakened. The most efficient viruses are airborn ones not ones that transmit through biting else we would have seen multiple zombie-like epidemics throughout history. Real life zombies in nature are more often the result of parasitic infection since parasites can't really be airborn, behavior-altering parasites are a real thing that turns hosts into the closest thing we have to zombie-like behavior. Parasitoid wasps, nematodes, fungi, bacteria and many more can create living zombies but it's often confined to invertebrates,  with the notable exception of certain fish and mammal hosts. The only known behavior-altering parasite to infect humans so far is Toxoplasma gondii and the effects are still unclear... There have been reports of some flu viruses making infected more social to spread the disease but more research is needed!

Hey Matpat, I'm sure this will be lost in the sea of comments, but I have an important theory regarding Super Mario 64. Don't stop reading, because I have some juicy evidence to back it up. Here it goes: the villain of the game is Peach and not Bowser. This might be surprising, because it seems obvious that Bowser is the villain. However, my theory is that Peach used the star power to assume the form of Bowser. Consider this: what are the in-game effects of wielding the star power? First and foremost is the ability to change shape and warp reality, as seen with various bosses given portions of the star power. There's also the ability to speak to Mario "telepathically" without being physically present. Obviously, these both apply to Bowser. Let's see how they apply to Peach. Does she change shape/warp reality? Well, yes. At the end of the game, she appears floating outside the castle. How does she appear? The star taken from Bowser transforms into Peach. We're led to believe that Bowser locked Peach up somehow and that the star power is the key to release her, but what if Bowser being "defeated" was just Peach transforming into the star form and then back into Peach? That's not conclusive evidence, but I have more. There's also the matter of telepathic speech. Obviously, Bowser can do this, but what about other characters? There are a few others. For one, Big Boo's Haunt includes telepathic speech, presumably from the Boo(s) that had stars. There are occasional instructional popups in various worlds, which could just be from Lakitu himself. However, there's one other character that speaks telepathically: Peach. At various points in the game such as Peach's Secret Slide, Peach communicates telepathically to Mario, a power that seems to be reserved for wielders of star power. So it seems plausible that Peach could have been using the star power, but we'll need a little more evidence to prove that she did. My next piece of evidence is the note at the beginning of the game, which says, "Dear Mario: Please come to the castle. I've baked a cake for you. Yours truly, Princess Toadstool." Based on the timing and context of how this is displayed, it's assumed that it was sent and delivered shortly before the intro cutscene, and that Mario left immediately for Peach's castle. We know this because it says she already baked the cake, which she wouldn't say if the letter would take days to deliver. It almost reads like a text message in terms of its timing. There are a couple problems with this. If Peach's letter is to be believed, then in the short interval between the letter being sent and Mario's arrival, Bowser arrived at the castle, overtook the entire thing, found where the star power was hidden, used the star power to bring most of the paintings to life, entered the paintings to give stars to bosses and hide the rest, created various traps in the castle, and still had time to greet Mario at the door. That seems suspiciously like it would take a long time. I'll get back to that in a moment, but there's another problem with the letter: the cake. Peach had said she baked a cake for us, yet the cake is nowhere to be found in the castle. Even when we "rescue" Peach, she tells us that she's going to bake a cake for us, as in she hasn't even baked it yet. This confirms that at the very least, the cake is a lie. There was never any cake waiting for us at the castle. So why did she say there was? This brings me to the part where I tie it all together. Peach was bored and wanted some adventure, so she used the star power to transform into Bowser and bring all those worlds to life. Then, after visiting each one and giving some extra star power to the bosses, she wanted even more adventure. That's when she sent a letter to Mario promising cake if he comes to the castle. She lied to him to get him to come to the castle and play along with her game. She wanted another adventure so much that she deliberately set up a crisis for Mario to rescue her from. Peach played the whole thing off as if Bowser captured her when she was behind it all.

At least she followed through with the cake.

They can both be used to tell a story (especially for RPGs), only the means to do so is different—, you'd say Toby is the *author/writer* and Gaster is the *narrator.*

Those are two different roles, but both are in charge of the diegesis to some extent, which is (in a way) what could usually be called world-building. 
That also shines a light on Gastor's presence/absence in his own narration: some narrators place themselves in their stories and some don't—but some stories _need their narrator to be present in it_ to make sense or to elicit the desired feelings in the reader/gamer.

I think that personally, both the Gaster-Toby Connection and the Kris-Toby connection could also be two sides of the same coin. When one creates a story, it often involves creating a world. You essentially become "The God of This World" and have complete control over it and all other canonical versions of that world, this would be the Gaster angle. As a story teller, exploring the different avenues and routes that can come with creating an entire world. But then, as a story teller, you must be careful not to let your story consume you. Many story tellers, especially with dedicated fan bases feel immense pressure to satisfy their fans and create the perfect story over and over again. This can often lead to sleepless nights, poor health, and in essence, ripping one's own soul out. I think that Toby Fox is writing his stories in parallel. This is of course, fairly obvious because he's created two games that are, themselves, parallel worlds, with parallel and opposite themes. The thing is, if the Gaster-Toby Connection and the Kris-Toby Connection are also a dichotomy, you might consider this fact. The G-T connection is a representation of how Toby felt creating Undertale. Everyone loved it, obsessed over it. He was the God of that world, the person who created the perhaps, not perfect in execution, but perfect in concept and reception, game, first try. But he wanted to do it again. However, he felt immense pressure when looking to create a new game. This pressure ate him alive, the feeling of not being good enough, the feeling of being a one trick pony. He continued to work however, building the dichotomy of his feelings as the creator of a world, as he built Deltarune. He put emphasis on a much more grand and impressive execution, but with less in the way of concept, and also in reception, which he expected and appears to have come to terms with. The game is far more beautiful and impressive in its art, music, and character writing (don't @ me, this is for the sake of explanation), but it was far less impressive in its concept, since the game is, of course, incomplete. The game Deltarune, unlike Undertale, which is a full game, doesn't have enough time to fully explore its mirror concept and idea of "your choices don't matter". I'm sure this will eventually change as the entire game is released, but as a writer, myself, I can totally understand the fear that what you create won't be good enough. Maybe I'm just looking too far into Toby's own creative struggle that may have made its way into the games, but it just seems like too much of an idea to pass up.

I definitely understand Toby when he states that he wakes up in the middle of the night unable to go back to sleep again. He’s definitely gotten the rockier path when it comes to the expression of creativity: creating a masterpiece on the first try. 

Usually, people start at the bottom and make their way up, building a history on their project/journey. Toby, and surely many others, have gotten the opposite: skipping the journey and creating something of high quality on the first try. Bear with me here. To make something where no one can give you (enough) criticism to make the next project even better, is definitely going to mess you up mentally if you wanna be the very best. Hell, I also think Toby separated Deltarune into chapters to see how well received chapter 1 was going to be, as a reassurance to keep going. 

Deltarune is an alternate universe for Undertale, not a sequel. Toby should be very proud of this decision. He now has a wide variety of options to work with, and seeing that he added a “dark world” and “light world” instead of keeping it the same with a “monster world” and “surface world”, he knows that this was a smart and safe decision in terms of catering to expectations.

Okay, a lot of MatPat theories are usually hit or miss for me, but I actually REALLY like this. As someone who's played Adventure in Ultimate, someone who was a bit confused by Master Core and its various forms in Smash 4, and as someone whose first Smash experience was Brawl and playing through The Subspace Emissary, this makes a lot of sense. I never play these games as someone demanding a certain character in the roster or to show off, I play them because they're fun and they have tons of heart and dedication poured into them. Adventure in Ultimate just re-solidified that for me, in a rather beautiful way. 

ALSO; Galeem being the big corporate entity and Dharkon being toxic fandom makes sense in each of their realms too– in the world of light, things are all laid out and orderly, like a standard progressive story mode, and it convinced you that Galeem is your end goal, when he's not. In contrast, the dark realm is made of broken pieces smashed together as if there was some kind of apocalpyse, arranged in a way that doesn't really make sense– giant cogwheels leading to broken streets leading to paths made of graphical errors, a representation of what the game would be if the fans were in control, being as disorderly and convoluted in their desires as they are.

Heck - even some of the ELDERLY here play Pokémon Go (which actually makes sense considering how watered down Pokémon Go is compared to other games in the franchise). Joey’s twisted symbolic story broken down.

Chapter 1 - The beginning of it all. The collection of the 6 items is the creation of the studio and the activation of the ink machine is the kickstart of the cartoons. Ink fills the studio to signify the swamping of work and so Henry dips. Joey appears as monster Bendy to try and make Henry stay and fails.

Chapter 2 - What happened after Henry left. We look through the eyes of one of the workers, Sammy Lawrence the music writer, to get an idea of the working conditions. It’s bad; there are pipes that just burst ink and flood the place, which could either be taken literally, or are a representation of the workload Joey puts on them. The story of Sammy is one I’m on the fence with. As the music writer, he is a key important employee for a studio about silent cartoons. He worships demon Bendy, Joey Drew, but he did something to make Joey angry. My theory is that with the difficult working conditions making writing music hard for him and the upkeep on demand, he plagiarised someone’s work and tried to offer it up, as symbolised by a ritual sacrifice. But it fails, and Joey’s not happy. I’m happy to hear other theories on what happened with Sammy.

Also around this time, a new character called Alice Angel is made without any input from Henry, and Susie Campbell is hired for her voice and she’s hype.

Chapter 3 - Internal strife and profit troubles. Alice just isn’t hitting it off with the public, probably doesn’t have that magic Henry touch like Bendy and Boris (like seriously, Alice only has ONE poster? She fell flat fast). Unsold dolls of Alice are making the company a loss. Thinking her voice is the reason, they prepare a replacement, Allison Pendle.

Susie is rightfully angry, being fired behind her back, but she might have also been a difficult person to work with. This is her first lead role and she might have gone overboard with it, making demands just like she did with Henry. She also grows an ego and begins looking down on other characters, for she’s rather condescending to the Butcher gang and she tears apart Boris.

Also around this time, Joey’s getting corrupt and beginning to grow cynical from his tape in the demon route.

Chapter 4 - Susie’s pissed. I think before her firing, she was doing something underhanded to either hurt the studio that burned her or to change, since she left that tape with the threatening tone of “you don’t make angels angry”. I think she was sabotaging Boris somehow, saying she “took what she needed” from him. But eventually the switch was made and Allison takes Susie’s place as Alice. Just maybe too late,

Also around this time, Bertrum is introduced with the production of Bendy Land in an effort to stay relevant. Bertrum’s pretty into making it, though he wants others to stay out of his business. But the plans fall through and Bertrum’s angry at his wasted time. This is also an introduction of the Ink People, workers that have been swamped with work and the studio is dragging them down. The Studio is now officially failing and nothing can save it.

Chapter 5 - Henry’s chapter, the end and the present. The journey to forgiveness. Sammy wasn’t fired yet and continued to stay in the studio, though driven insane. I think that part is literal, work made him insane. The workers attack when Sammy leaves as he was probably one of the last OG member of the studio left; Henry quit, Wally probably finally made good on his promise and got outta there, and they hound Allison and Tom to leave and end the studio.

Henry is reintroduced into Joey’s life. Allison and Tom, her husband, form a friendship with him while on Joey’s path to mending. Allison is nice enough, offering him food, while Tom is more reluctant, probably seeing him as a friend that abandoned Joey in his time of need. Allison sometimes sides with her husband though, symbolised by “she’ll leave you for dead”. It’s a rocky friendship.

Eventually, they leave it up to him to finish closing the book on Joey’s regrets as they can’t; they are a part of the worst era of Joey’s life while Henry got out before it got to that point. Henry goes in and shows Joey “the end”, but the cycle repeats because regret is hard to shake off. But he’a getting there. That’s good.

Nice lesson about bees, MatPat... but you're ignoring all the evidences we have that Peach is, in fact, human:

1) The "Mushroom King" was an invention made by Nintendo of America for the SMB instruction booklet.
He was never present in any Japanese material and that's the reason we don't see him in the games.
That's also why his presence in supplemental guides and comics didn't last long. He never was canon. Same with the queen.
Also, the fact that the King uses a Mushroom head in the picture of that guidebook is just a simple deviant drawing made by the author of the book.  Since he was never invented, they didn't had a design to base him. For example, in the Nintendo Comic System series, there was another version of the Mushroom King, and he was clearly human.

2) The "Grandma" character from Super Mario RPG isn't really Peach's grandmother.
She was simply a elderly maid in the Japanese version of the game. That's was Woolsey's fault. (the game's translator/localizer)

3) We've seem Baby Peach multiple times and she isn't a Toad.

4) Peachette has grey eyes because Toadette has them too. (look closely in some more recent artwork and you'll see it).
Not because she's still an infant. She's clearly an adult. We've seem children Toads in RPGs, they're shorter.
The grey simply indicate that she's Toadette. It's the same logic why enemies in Super Mario Odyssey have blue eyes when Mario possesses them.

5) Toads aren't genderless. All Koichi Hayashida said was "We never really went out of our way to decide on the sex of these characters, even though they have somewhat gendered appearances". He's just implying that when they created the character, way back in 1985, they didn't decided Toad's gender, but it's obvious that when the time passed, Toad was clearly a boy.
Toads do have genders, just like humans. We've seem it in multiple games. He never stated that they are gendeless or that they took gendered roles as they wished. Gamespot misinterpreted this information (or made it on purpose to have a clickbait article) and this false statement spread like the plague all over the internet. 

6) It seems only Toadette can get the Super Crown in the game. The other characters just get coins.
That alone makes the theory senseless because there are no other Toadettes. We have other female Toads, but just ONE Toadette. She's a character.

7) Until Nintendo says otherwise, I'm pretty sure the port isn't canon. Super Mario 64 DS was never re-acknowledged by Nintendo in other Mario games, witch means the original SM64 is the true version of that tale.

Your analysis on Sparta is almost entirely inaccurate albeit its not really your fault. Sparta originated as a Cretan invasion force and throughout its history this fact was never forgotten. The Spartans considered themselves superior than the "Helots" they conquered and set up a caste hierarchy with the native Greeks being kept as slaves while the spartan citizens were effectively nobility. Over time Sparta gained very VERY many slaves in their empire with slaves outnumbering spartan citizens almost 9-1. This did two things: one was Spartan citizens became fabulously wealthy and two they became notoriously cautious. Since the helots outnumbered the Spartans by such a large margin and the Sparta made no effort to integrate the foreigners slave revolt was a constant threat. Any large defeat on the battlefield could mean not enough troops to keep the Helots down and so Sparta didn't expand beyond their peninsula in anything but influence. Also due to this Sparta invested heavily in propaganda and military equipment. They weren't the strongest fighters and were very cautious relying on mercenaries, alliances and their generals to minimize casualties which worked and after 300 (which was actually a broad alliance of numerous smaller city states and Sparta who decided to stay behind and was actually closer to 1200) they did become feared. They pushed this one battle so hard and spread so many lies about their culture (impossible to correct since Sparta was closed off tighter than north korea at the time) that they turned from the rich Cretan nobles with weird quirky laws to the ultimate warriors. But in reality they were a mix between a landed aristocracy and a wealthy militia. Their reputation held because they almost never fought wars with Athens being the main aggressor in most wars in Greece. Once they did finally take a serious unavoidable loss their empire collapsed and they became even more like north korea: an impoverished hyper militaristic state desperately trying to survive against the Athenian and Macedonian superpowers. In short they were never like what they were depicted as in 300 or in their propaganda and even only held that reputation for about 250 years but since those 250 years are the most well documented and dynamic period in Greek history the stereotype remains.

Looking at the pictures of the rackets breaking apart and at their shape, I think it is more likely that the Rackets are made from wood. A little research shows that Ash is a fairly common wood that is used to make wooden rackets, it has a shear Strength of 10 MPa. 

Secondly, the racket acts as a lever. In this case I would treat it as a Cantilever. I don't have the expertise to count pixels and compare, but for sake of argument lets say the racket is 72 cm, this falls in regulation size and judging from the screen shots the racket is about 1/2 the size of Mario, it also makes for easier math. The "sweet spot" for a tennis racket can vary, how ever, if we assume that it is 1/4 of the way from the top of the racket and that the top of Mario's hand is 1/4 from the bottom that would mean we have a cantilever with a length of 360mm.

To find the force exerted on the racket at the top of Mario's hand we use (Force*lengthFromOrgin)/CrossSection = (65N*360mm)/740mm^2 = 31.622N/mm^2 = 31.622 MPa

Meaning the 65N the ball generates is about 3 times the force needed to break a racket made of Ash wood. Of course an actual racket would be made of laminated wood, for which I could not find a shear strength of and would vary greatly anyway depending on the adhesives used. Then again, it is 3am, I may be wrong about all of that.

As somebody who's worked with 3d models I know it's much easier to animate the racket coming apart at a segmented piece such as near the handle. So in your joke about being too hard to implement in the game is somewhat true as it happens so quick so wouldn't have to be as precise looking in-game and is only shown to represent it happening compared to promo photos which use higher quality models that are pre-rendered and don't have to worry about causing lag as they're just photos. It's like claiming the balls used to represent Mario's hands in 64 are what his actual hands look like and not just a representation do to limitation. This just shows despite rapidly advancing hardware, cuts like these made to only represent something and not it's exact physical properties in their world are still being made today, whether it be time constraints, memory, stylistic, or just not wanting to spend hours of modeling individual pieces and keeping a low poly count on the base model to improve stability. Long story short it's more likely promo images are more trustworthy to go on as it's more likely to better represent what's actually supposed to be happing as the modelers have a lot more control and less restraints on properly portraying what's actually happening in them. (However not all promo pics and renders are perfect since cloth generators, alpha channels, etc can act a little goofy and when you're rendering an extremely high resolution model it takes a long time and a lot of money so if something small messes up the company may just chose to use the image anyways rather than go back into the model, try to edit the issue and not make it worse and then hope it's fixed for the next render attempt.) Of course I'm no professional but going off my own experiences I really believe that's what's actually happening here.

Matt, I like your "game hypothesis", but I think the story comes together nicely if it's a bar. Why? Because if Afton wasn't able to get into the bar, that must mean he was already kicked out from drinking too much. (This is further hinted at by his behavior upon arriving home). The implications of this are huge. This would mean that when Afton murdered the girl who became the puppet, he was in a drunken rage. Which means he probably regretted killing her. While this at first seems unlikely, think about it. The first death we know of after Henry's daughter is Elizabeth (aka Baby). The existence of Baby and the fun-time animatronics, who were designed to lure off children for Afton to gather remnant from, implies Afton was trying to resurrect someone. A big question for me has always been who though. My guess is that he designed those animatronics in order to bring Henry's daughter back. It also explains why he's so angry at seeing his youngest son ran off to Fredbear's: he's worried his son was at the site of his murder. He in fact was, which lead to his trauma and fear of returning to the restaurant.
Most importantly though, I think this timeline explains how Michael survived and why he's confused over his own name. I think after the incident with Elizabeth and Baby, Afton realized for the first time the full impact of remnant: that it allowed it's deceased owner to live on through a physical host. Coincidentally, Michael died a short while later. However, if remnant could allow a deceased person to live on through ANY host, it makes sense that Afton wouldn't want his Michael to live on through a robot like his sister. So my theory is he picked a human host for Michael to live on through instead. To clarify, he infused an already living human with the remnant of his dead son. For me , this suddenly explains a lot:

1. If Michael was the crying child from 1983, how was he of working age by Fnaf 1 and 2? My belief is that his new "host" body was much older.
2. His confusion in the logbook over who he is. If he was sharing a body with his host's original consciousness, he might have eventually realized who he really was: not originally Michael, although he had all those memories.
3. Why he didn't die after being gutted by the scooper. The truth is, Michael was no longer really alive at that point. He was just a body filled with remnant. Killing the host didn't kill him: he just became a corpse full of remnant.

The flaws here are obvious;
for the one thing, the Boris that we hang-out with in Chapter 3, isn't the Tom-Boris that we meet at the end of Chapter 4; it's the Disfigured Boris that Alice makes us fight at the end of the Haunted House ride. (which is kind of disappointing, considering this chapter was built-up around SAVING him.)
So regardless, what we knew about the original Boris makes sense for him to be Wally; he still knows enough to dismantle certain mechanics - like the lever for the door - and knows his way while crawling around through the vents; so it makes sense that he's a maintenance man like Wally.

In a way though, I think I believe what you say that Henry is "destined" to be the "Perfect Bendy"...but in a lot of ways, I also think that's why Joey - Bendy - is trying to kill him.
You have to consider the problem with your theory; if what you say is true, and Joey Drew ISN'T Bendy, then that means that Joey - who is of such SIGNIFICANT importance, to the lore of the game - so far hasn't made a SINGLE appearance. That's just bad story-telling.
Plus, in a lot of ways, the Cartoon Character you become in this place sort of represents where you were - your position of power or recognition, or even your actions - during your time working for the company.
Susie and Alison both become Alice Angels because they were both tied to the character at one point; but because Susie is overcome with hatred and jealousy towards Alison, her Angel is imperfect and distorted.
Norman Polk is the guy who ran the Projection-Booth, so he became the Projectionist; I wonder if it was intentional on his part, as maybe he just came out as a blobby-Ink Person, but attached the projector to his head, because it was so familiar to him in life.
Bertrum Piedmont becomes one of the Carnival Rides - the very ride he himself was designing; like something out of a Tim Burton-esque Beauty and the Beast.
And Tom and Wally are both maintenance workers and clean-up crew...Effectively their job is to obey orders; to go to each location and do as they are told...Almost like Dogs; plus they're ultimately friendly and loyal - Tom being worried about safety with the Elevators, and Wally never abandoning the place, despite claiming to be "Outta Here." So of course, they'd take the form of Bendy's Sidekick Boris.
Sammy and the other workers in the facility are the face-less ones; the ones who didn't have much notoriety or respect. As Sammy himself stated in Chapter 2, no one really appreciates his craft, or considers it work - especially to the point where Joey put a pump to drain the stairwell in his office, meaning that people were constantly coming in and out all day. Plus, I doubt anyone really liked Sammy too much.
Because of this, Sammy - like so many others - didn't have enough of an impact to become a distinctive character, and are just trapped as humanoid blobs, desperate to get out...

And then there's Joey Drew himself - the head-honcho. The guy who pretends to be all about inspiring people to go for their dreams, while being unable to stomach the platitudes himself; the guy who dreams up plans and ideas and forces others to make them a reality, the guy who steals other people's work in order to promote himself...The guy who built and installed the Ink Machine in the first place...

I am certain the reason Joey did this, was in an attempt to escape death, his own weakness, and achieve immortality by becoming his Animated Character Mascot, Bendy. But then, why is he corrupt?
Take notice of how the walls will sometimes have, "The Creator Lied to Us." written on them...
That's a reference to how Joey took credit for being the creator of Bendy, when all he did was steal it from Henry. The reason that Henry is important, is because he is the TRUE creator of Bendy. Therefore, because Joey lied, the ritual did not work, and his Bendy form is imperfect and deformed...In fact, I believe the reason that Joey collected the Projectionist, is because he is doing much the same that Alice did - he's trying to fix himself; achieve perfection by stealing the Ink and Insides of other ink-character monsters in the building...that's why he goes after Sammy FIRST before attacking you...But at the end of the day, he's still trying to get you - because he believes...something...

Consider the fact that this has long since happened before Henry received the letter...and the Ink Machine was turned off. My guess is, that when the Ink stopped flowing, most of the characters were trapped inside the pipes and couldn't escape. Someone had to have turned the Ink Machine off, or maybe the ritual failed because Henry was not present...
Maybe that's why Joey sent Henry the letter, asking him to come by the studio and see everything...and that's why Henry had to gather up the items to place on the pedestals to perform the Ink Machine Ritual - he needed to provide something of his OWN in order to properly appease whatever "god" is causing all of this...the bottle of pen ink...

Now that the REAL creator has returned, I see one of two possibilities...
1; that Henry will become a Perfect Bendy and manage to save everyone, putting them to rest, like you said...
Or 2; that Joey is going to try to use Henry's body - to assimilate him into his Inky-Form in order to become a Perfect Bendy himself.

Looking closely at the game footage Sonic is not transferring all of that force into just his legs. He bends at the waist, putting energy into his core muscles to allow him to rapidly accelerate in the opposite direction. In addition, he shifts his arms, changing his center of gravity and allowing gravity to counter some of the forces. While doing all of that, he is also using his inertia to turn as he slows down, further shifting the forces. He then uses the remaining redirected inertial energy in combination with the energy stored in his muscles and the force of gravity to begin his running in the opposite direction. All of this means that, as a first order approximation your calculations make sense but the reality is counterintuitive and those calculations don't reflect the proper spherical cow.

EDIT: Get ready for some real physics (keeping it newtonian though)

Let's assume all of the numbers are right except for the position of the comet on day 10
We'll give the comet no relative velocity at the start to see the minimum damage

Some variables:
G= gravitational constant = 6.67 x 10^-11 (SI units)
R= Radius of Venus = 6,052,000 m
r= distance of comet from the centre of Venus = 15,569 + 6,052,000 m 
M= mass of Venus = 4.867 x 10^24 Kg
m= mass of comet = 400,000 Kg 

The gravitational field strength varies as the distance from the planet changes so just plugging in speed= acceleration*time doesn't work out. Luckily energy conservation always holds true and it'll help us out for this. (I'm not explaining the formulae, finish high school)

The gravitational potential energy of the comet in space = -GMm/r
The kinetic energy of the comet in space = 0

The gravitational potential energy of the comet on the surface = -GMm/R
The kinetic energy of the comet just at the surface = 1/2mv^2

Thanks to energy conservation we can simply equate the energy
-GmM/r + 0 = -GMm/R + 1/2mv^2

Rearranging, we get 1/2mv^2=GMm(1/R - 1/r)

Now by plugging in all the numbers we get the kinetic energy of the comet to be 5.5 x 10^10 J

I'm sorry. I screwed up with this one. In a few facts and details, certainly, but also in ways that I didn't expect when writing it. And I don't want things to be taken the wrong way, so please, let me clarify:

First, the intro was not intended to make fun of or belittle the fanbase of Persona in any way, and I'm sorry if it came across as mean spirited. Being protective of a franchise isn't a bad thing. I know from doing episodes on franchises like Dark Souls that there are just fanbases who are more amenable to theorizing than others and by choosing this episode, no matter what I would say, it would make some people angry (even if the facts had all been straight, which again, some weren't). I wrote that intro trying to play up the joke that it was a video no one would like, and in the process, I created a self-fulfilling prophesy that offended people and I'm sorry about that. It's never my intent to offend people. Maybe poke fun of in a joking way or call out for bad behavior (some other YouTubers), but it's never my goal to offend a group of people for liking what they like -- I'm sorry if it came off that way.

Second, I clearly didn't go deep enough or understand everything as clearly as I thought I did. As with the Phoenix Wright episode (another misjudgment on my part), I thought this game would function well-enough as a stand-alone title, but clearly there were added details in other games as well as supplemental content that I just didn't take into consideration. There were a few facts in this one that I either forgot to double check because I assumed I knew them off the top of my head (Elizabeth) or I could have explained better (Izanami). Again, I should have gone deeper, but time constraints and thinking I had covered all the necessary ground made me stop looking when clearly I should have kept digging.

Third, sorry for being defensive. My life this past weekend was incredibly stressful and sad, so having a video receive a heavy backlash in the middle of it all was the last thing I needed, which resulted in me losing my head. Please remember that I receive hundreds of comments every day telling me how awful I am as a person and how I should die because I said X about Y character and that 99% of the time I let it run off me, but sometimes it just gets to you. This weekend was one of those times, so I ask you to forgive that brief saltiness.

And lastly, regarding how I handle criticism, I want you to know that I'm listening. All the time. I read the comments, and yes, I don't respond a lot because when I have in the past, people have taken my responses the wrong way. Instead, I take your comments to heart and try to adjust the programming and scripts on the channel accordingly. Heck, this whole episode was in an effort to try and address some people who were tired of hearing about the same franchises over and over again. 

It's a bit of a Catch-22. My policy always was "Read the criticism and make changes to the series based on the feedback, but never directly call it out." That only prompted a lot of backlash of people saying "He doesn't acknowledge criticism." So, I've tried addressing negativity in a public way, but people criticized me for doing that too saying I was "bad at taking criticism" because I did that. It often feels like a lose-lose situation. 

Just know that I'm not writing this to be defensive, but to sincerely apologize for the mistakes in this video, the lack of clarity in some of the jokes, and to promise you that I will continue to work at getting better about all these issues. - MatPat

Firstly: "his assistant Elizabeth"... Wrong game Mat, that was Persona 3. In Persona 4 the assistant is Margaret.

Both Adachi and Yu awakened to their persona to survive in the TV world as a result of Izanami. (Namatame would have as well, but he never had the chance to do so). As a Persona can never return to being a shadow, it is impossible for their shadows to exist as long as the user as a Persona. Finally - we DO see Yus shadow. In the final episode of the Anime, we see that Yu DOES have a shadow as he is hounded by it during the Margaret fight until he accepts it. The reason why Yu does not normally face his shadow is that Izanami awakened it for him. As soon as Izanami wanted him dead in the anime, he lost it and had to face his own shadow properly to get it back. 

I'm sorry Mat, but you really didn't do the research on this one. Granted, for a series so full of lore, it is easy to miss facts, and the hypothesis is rather interesting - but it is rather full of holes and you made several mistakes - both relevant and non relevant.

When I was 16 years old, I was going to kill myself. I had a plan. I had the time, the place, the way I would do it. I didn't want to be alive anymore. My boyfriend had dumped me, I was off my medication, and my family was having trouble paying bills. I thought I would be of more help to others if I were dead. I felt like I was deadweight, like I was worthless. All of this happened in December of 2015 and January of 2016. I had started watching GTLive in June of 2015. For a long time, GTLive literally was the ONLY thing that kept me from jumping off of the 2nd story balcony of my highschool. I'm one timezone hour behind MatPat, so GTLive happens at 3 PM for me. My high school got out at 2:15. For a long time, the only thing that I felt I had to live for was to see Mat and Steph on the couch together, talking to me, playing video games, and treating me like I was worth something. Every day, I would go through the school day to be able to hang out with Mat and Steph. They were the only people who I felt I wasn't a nuisance to. They don't even know I exist. I'm one of millions of people. But it gave me something to live for, something to fight for. In March of that year, I started making YouTube videos. This gave me one more thing to fight for. Even if it was fighting simply so that I could upload the video I had made the night before, it was something to fight for. Weekends were hard. My parents' WiFi stinks, quite frankly, we couldn't afford unlimited, and it would take 3 hours to upload a 30 minute gameplay video. As a result, I would use the school WiFi to upload my videos. I would upload twice a week, Tuesdays and Thursdays. Combining no uploads with no GTLive, weekends were very difficult for me. There was many a Saturday where I wanted to give up, where I wanted to stop fighting. Then a little voice would say, "But Katie, if you give up, you'll miss GTLive! Don't you wanna watch Scary Games Friday?" It may seem stupid, but that is how I was able to comfort myself. I kept fighting, and slowly, very slowly, I finally was able to feel alive again. I may not have killed myself physically, but for a long time, I was dead. Emotionally, mentally, cognitively. The only way I was alive was in the medical sense. So Mat, and Steph, and Jason, and everyone. Thank you. If it weren't for you, I would be in a casket, 6 feet under, with every bone in my body crushed from jumping 10-15 feet off the balcony where I had my first kiss. Thank you for saving me. I know it's hard to understand, but you guys saved me. You really did.

Mat, you probably won't read this comment. Considering you look for theorists on Reddit, and this comment was posted a year after this video. But, I've tried coming up with some scales.

There's no way to get a good sense of scale from the locations we visit in odyssey. If we measure their area, we'll have no idea how big they are compared to Mario's planet... But, we have an ace up our sleeve! Or in this case, an ace in the back of our closets. So dust off your GameCube, (or Wii) because we're going to Isle Delfino!

If we look at promotional material and other maps for odyssey, you might see a familiar island beside the Mushroom Kingdom. It has the signature, and bizarrely coincidental shape of a dolphin. Other people might see it as hints for a return to sunshine in odyssey DLC, but for now I'm seeing it as a perfect measuring tool. 

Scaling the island has the same issue as odyssey's kingdoms; we don't know the size of visitable locations compared to each other, or the rest of the land. But there's one spot on sunshine's island that lets us scale all of Delfino, and maybe the rest of the planet. Delfino Airstrip. Looking at the in-game map of the island, we see that the airstrip is on a small piece of land, in an L shape. (Luigi approved) But rather than the airstrip being a small location on that L, that L is the entire airstrip. The L has the same basic shape, and scale of the airstrip.

If we use Mario as a ruler, we can find the area of the airstrip. It's completely flat plain, so we probably won't have too many issues. With the airstrip's area found, we can look at the island's map; and use the airstrip to find the area of Delfino. With Delfino's area, we can compare it to other kingdoms from odyssey; letting us find the surface area of the whole planet!

But of course, there will be some measuring issues; because of map inconsistencies. Take for example, Earth. If you make a 2D map of Earth, it won't be a completely reliable one. The Earth is a sphere, so creating a flat map of it is impossible to perfect. There will always be angle, and size inconsistencies. BUT, if you have a smaller map of something like a city or an island, the scale becomes consistent due to only slight curvature of the locations. So, the in-game map of Delfino is consistent to the actual island; both size and scale wise.

This measurement may be a bit crude, and kind of difficult to pull off, but you might be able to use this to measure Mario's planet!

Mario Odyssey’s World should be around 11.7 times smaller than Earth. 
Now, give me a moment as I’m doing this during a break from studying for finals and the only thing moving me is caffeine. 
First let’s make some assumptions.
1. The planet’s air density is 15kg/m3 as compared to Earth’s as referenced by Austin’s SCIENCE video.
2. The planet has equivalent atmospheric composition such as particulates, molecular composition, and atmospheric layers. 
3. It’s Sun is the same temperature as our own. 
4. It’s inhabitants have eyes that view the same visible spectrum as us.
The linchpin of my assumption is Rayleigh Scattering. 
Rayleigh scattering is the elastic scattering of electromagnetic radiation by particles smaller than their wavelength. Scattering is heavily wavelength dependent, so shorter wavelengths(blues) are scattered more strongly than longer wavelengths(reds). 
It is also heavily dependent on air density and thickness of the atmosphere. The thickness of Earth’s the atmosphere is roughly 100 km or 62 miles as defined by the Kármán Line, about 1.57% of the earths radius. At noon and through most of the day our sky is blue because it is traveling through the 62 miles of 1.275 kg/m3 atmosphere but at sunrise/sunset the light from the sun must travel through more of the total atmosphere and specifically more atmosphere closer to earth where the air density is higher, increasing the scattering further, reddening the light. 
Now there are several variables that influence the color of the sky, which is why I made assumptions of the planet’s atmosphere being as our own. 
So, including all assumptions and basing my conclusion principally on the atmospheric effects of Rayleigh scattering I start throwing down the digits.
Earths Kármán Line is 100km equaling 1.57% of its radius. Its air density is 1.275 kg/m3. It’s shape is roughly a sphere. 
Assuming the Mario planet has an air density of 15, it is 11.76 times denser than earth’s. Assuming density and atmospheric thickness have an inverse relationship to Rayleigh scattering effects we divide our 100km Kármán like of earth to the Mario planet’s times greater density of 11.76 to get a Kármán line of 8.5 km assuming it has proportional layers to earth and if dividing that 8.5 km K-Line by the Earths proportionate K-Line fraction of 1.67% we get a total radius of,
Drumroll please, 541.4 km or a circumference of 3,399.203 km. For reference the Earth’s moon is around 10,921 km. Now, that is not truly feasible as a the planet would not be able to exist. It doesn’t have enough gravity at earth’s density to sustain an atmosphere. Hmmm, coffee break.

Screw it, let’s increase it’s density. 
Density is mass/volume. So by increasing mass but keeping volume constant, we can increase the gravity of an object. For earths normal gravity on the Mario planet we’d multiply earth’s density of 5.51g/cm3 to the 11.76 proportionate atmosphere thickness number earlier(Skipping all the conversion explanations)  to give us a density of 64.80 g/cm3 would give a planet with suitable mass be habitable.

So massive portions of the planet would be Gold and other heavy matter, even Star matter.

I have a definitive story now.

Henry and William are business partners. They create sister location, with Baby Ballora and the funtimes. William warns his daughter Elizabeth not to go near Baby, but she does anyway. Baby then opens up her stomach and kills her (as seen in the SL minigame). This causes it to be shutdown after only one day. Ballora doesn't seem to have pre recorded lines like the fun times, but more human-like dialogue like Baby. And, in the Freddy's survival guide, it shows a song sung by Ballora that leads us to believe she is the mother, Mrs. Afton. The SL animatronics are stored underground.
After SL is shut down, Fazbear Entertainment buys out the other animatronic corporations, bringing Chica into the gang. FNaF 4 location opens and it leads to the Bite of 83. Crying Child, or Micheal, is dying as you play as him in FNaF 4. Psychic Friend FredBear is Cassidy. All of the animatronics in FNaF 4 are imaginary, but Nightmare, or Old Man Consequence, signifies death. When Mike dies, his father, William, promises that he will "put him back together." And he does, using remnant.
The bite of 83 causes springlock suits to get discontinued. At some point around this time, Charlie is killed on her birthday and goes on to posses the puppet. William, Fazbear Entertainment's technician uses the Springtrap suit to lure four children to the safe room where he kills them. One of the four children killed, Susie, was lured by William because he killed her dog so he could experiment with Remnant (leading to mangle), and William told Susie her dog was alive and to follow him. The four deaths cause the location to be shut down. The four children go on to posses Bonnie, Freddy, Chica, and Foxy.
Lots of time passes and then those four animatronics along with the puppet are moved to the FNaF two location for a new grand reopening. They are also there with Toy Chica, Toy Bonnie, Toy Freddy, and Mangle. All of those animatronics except Mangle are linked to a criminal database with facial recognition software trying to prevent murder. However, William strikes again and causes an investigation to take place. He was working as the day shift worker, but because of the investigation he flees and leave the position open. Jeremy Fitzgerald takes his place and is killed in what is known as the Bite of 87. 
Because of this bite, animatronics are no longer allowed to be able to free roam. The toy animatronics are scrapped, and the core four animatronics are brought to the original FNaF one location. Now William knows that the four are possessed and mad, so he tries to dismantle them in the safe room. But their spirits still live in without possessing animatronics, so William tries to hide from them using his murder suit, Springtrap. But in his panic, the springlocks fail, leading to Afton's death. Fazbear Entertainment tries to cover up his death by locking the safe room, leaving Afton inside of Springtrap. Remember this.
Micheal then goes to SL in an attempt to find his sister, Elizabeth. He does, because she is stored in Baby. But, he gets himself scooped in the process. He then is filled with Enards, but survives because of remnant. However, his body decays. Turning him, quite literally, purple. It's here at sister location when he realizes how evil his father was, and the murders he committed. So he goes on a mission to free all the spirits inside the animatronics. At SL, he begins to plan the family reunion at a future pizzeria, so he sets Enard (who contains Ballora) free, along with Baby, his sister.
He goes to the FNaF one location, where the core four still are and have been since FNaF two shut down. He tries to free the spirits, but is fired because of his odor (he's literally decaying) and because he's "tampering with the animatronics." He is also unable to free their spirits because the animatronics keep trying to kill him. Why? Because he looks just like his father. When Mike is at the FNaF location trying to free the spirits, Psychic Friend FredBear, or Cassidy, or Golden Freddy, tries to reach out to him. I'm not quite sure how Cassidy died, but it's not really important. Golden Freddy is a spirit, and not a physical animatronic, which is why he disappears and reappears almost like a hologram.
Now, when you get your pink slip in FNaF two as Fritz Smith you are told that you were fired on your first day on the job because of "Odor" and "Tampering With the Animatronics." Coincidence? No. Mike IS Fritz, and he's going location to location to try and free the spirits. But he can't. They're trying to kill him because he looks like his dad, William.
After failing at this, he tries to come find his father. Remember what I said earlier? He's still in the Springlock suit as Fazbear fright. So he goes to work as a security guard at Fazbear Fright. Afton, possessing Spring trap, keeps attacking him. To try and release his father's spirit, he burns the place down. However, Afton, who is now possessing Springtrap, is able to escape. However, this fire made the core four spirits to finally be released, because remember, overheating (aka fires) causes spirits to finally be laid to rest. That's exactly what happens, in the happiest day minigame. Now the only ones left to be laid to rest are Cassidy, Elizabeth (the Afton daughter), Ballora (the Afton mother), the puppet (Lefty is built by Mike to contain the puppet, which Lefty does), and William Afton. 
So Mike and Henry start this plan to put all of them in one place at the new and final pizzeria. In the salvage run where Mike salvages Molten Freddy (who is essentially Enard, containing Ballora), Baby, Springtrap (Afton) and Lefty (containing the puppet). Then, with help from Henry, Micheal burns the place down. Mike dies, and William goes to Hell. The Afton mother, the Afton daughter, and Charlie are finally laid to rest.
This leaves one more: Cassidy.
And finally, in the cutscene from Ultimate Custom Night, Cassidy speaks to Old Man Consequence. There she is told to stop fighting. That Micheal is dead, and she doesn't have to stick around for him. And so Cassidy goes, and she is laid to rest.
And that's where the story ends.

Hi. I'm a professional box maker. (kill me)
You made a big, massive mistake: NOBODY makes boxes that are this big, used for moving stuff, made of E flutes. (E has only a waveheight of 1.0–1.9 mm = Thickness, super flimsy and DEFINITELY not 0.45cm) They're either made of B, C or BC or maybe EB. (BC and EB is double walled stuff made of two different waves. Very common) In this case, just judging by the looks of it, I would say it is a C flute, with a grading of 1.30 to 1.50 and a waveheight of about 4mm.
This material grading is what we use in Europe to specify the strength of the material, different from ECT but directly correlated.  The ECT is independent of the kind if box-form used. (In this case it is a FEFCO 201)
The first digit describes the "number of walls/"wavy things" and the last two are some arbitrary quality indicators. (Higher = better) Details can be found in lists provided by the manufacturer of the corrugated board. I found this one, it's in German, but the last column is ECT (Kantenstauchwiderstand) in kN/m. http://www.horn-verpackung.de/wellpapp-qualitaten
Meaning that this box probably has a ECT of 4.5 to 6.5kN/m. (1.30 to 1.50)
A way bigger mistake however is that mistook the ECT rating for PSI. This is false. It actually means per linear inch: "This is measured in pounds per lineal inch of load bearing edge (lb/in), but usually reported as an ECT value (for example, 44 ECT)." https://www.theboxery.com/ect.asp
So... 4.5kN/m = 25.6lb/in and 6.5kN/m = 37.1lb/in. And that means to get PSI you need to include the waveheight and the thickness of the two top layers. A C-flute has a height of 3.1–4.0 mm and the two top layers add about 0.1mm so lets simply use 4mm. (C flute is usually more at the top end of this scale) 4 mm = 0.15748 in, using 1 ft as the foot length (why not) we get a area of 1.88976 in². (Lets forget the second foot since you always start with only one)
Lets be generous and use the material grade 1.50 with 37.1 lb/in (PLI) to calculate the PSI. I think it is: 37.1 lb/in * 1.88976 in² = 70.110096 psi .... But I am tired, need to sleep. Since you have to remake the entire video anyway you could also try to find a better conversion from PLI to PSI. :P
